extract:
侗族大歌（侗語：kgal laox，直译：「大歌」，漢字記音作「嘎老」；亦稱kgal mags，漢字記音作「嘎瑪」）是流傳於中華人民共和國西南地區侗族聚居區的一種多聲部、無指揮、無伴奏、自然合聲的民間合唱音樂形式。它是中國民間支聲複調音樂的代表之一，其源頭一般被追溯至古代百越人群的音樂實踐。宋代詩人陸游在《老學庵筆記》中便留下了早期合唱形式的文獻記載。侗族大歌以「眾低獨高」的聲部結構、對自然之聲的模擬以及獨特的調式特徵，引起了學術界的關注。1950年代，音樂學者在貴州省黎平縣岩洞村等地發現了這種音樂形式，向學術界證明中國民間確實存在無伴奏複音合唱，使學界修正了此前「中國傳統音樂沒有多聲部」的既有認識。2009年，聯合國教科文組織將侗族大歌列入人類非物質文化遺產代表作名錄。
侗族大歌主要流傳於使用侗語南部方言的貴州、廣西等省區。這一區域屬於典型的稻作耕種文化區，社會與自然系統保存得較為完整。侗族長期缺乏廣泛通行的本民族書寫系統，大歌主要依靠口傳，因而承擔了歷史傳承、道德規範與文化交流的功能。大歌的生存與發展，與侗族的社會空間及日常民俗活動密不可分。鼓樓、風雨橋等傳統建築，以及「行歌坐夜」、「月也」等社交儀式，共同構成了大歌發展的文化生態。在社會結構與親屬制度層面，大歌與當地的「姑舅表婚」制度、內婚集團邊界以及「陪姑田」等資源流動機制深度交織。傳統上，大歌主要包含鼓樓大歌、聲音大歌、柔聲大歌、倫理大歌、敘事大歌、禮俗大歌、童聲大歌、戲曲大歌與踩堂歌等類型。此外，當地還流傳著琵琶歌、牛腿琴歌、河歌以及侗戲等多種音樂形式。
隨著現代化、都市化與全球化的推進，侗族大歌的生存與傳承環境面臨著年輕一代侗語能力下降、傳統社交空間縮減等挑戰。為了保護這項文化遺產，中國政府、學術界與地方社區自20世紀末起展開了多方面的保育實踐。與此同時，大歌也在現代大眾傳媒的推動下，經歷了從傳統儀式向現代舞台景觀的轉型，並多次在海外進行文化交流與展演。
title: 侗族大歌

extract: The udug (Sumerian: 𒌜), later known in Akkadian as the utukku, were an ambiguous class of demons from ancient Mesopotamian mythology found in the literature of  Sumer, Akkad, Assyria and Babylonia. They were born in the underworld (Kur), as a beings different from the dingir (Anu-nna-Ki and Igigi), and they were generally malicious, even if a member of demons (Pazuzu) was willing to clash both with other demons and with the gods, even if he is described as a presence hostile to humans. The word is generally ambiguous and is sometimes used to refer to demons as a whole rather than a specific kind of demon. No visual representations of the udug have yet been identified, but descriptions of it ascribe to it features often given to other ancient Mesopotamian demons: a dark shadow, absence of light surrounding it, poison, and a deafening voice. The surviving ancient Mesopotamian texts giving instructions for exorcizing the evil udug are known as the Udug Hul texts. These texts emphasize the evil udug's role in causing disease and the exorcist's role in curing the disease.
title: Udug

extract:
Catherine Samba-Panza (née Souga; born 26 June 1954) is a Central African politician who served as Transitional President of the Central African Republic from 2014 to 2016. She was the first woman to serve as head of state in the Central African Republic. Prior to her tenure as acting president, she was the Mayor of Bangui from 2013 to 2014.
Samba-Panza began her career operating an insurance brokerage and working as a women's rights advocate. She was chosen in 2003 to serve as the vice president of a national reconciliation conference, and she was then chosen as president of the subsequent committee to implement the conference's recommendations. She was appointed mayor of Bangui in 2013 after the city was devastated by the Central African Republic Civil War. She was then appointed to serve as transitional president of the Central African Republic in 2014. She was tasked with restoring stability to the nation by disarming militant groups, and she emphasized the nation's economic recovery through employment and foreign aid. Her term ended in 2016. She was a presidential candidate in the 2020–21 election, but she was unsuccessful.
title: Catherine Samba-Panza
